Author-written notes: hemocyanin and cephalopod blood (general biology knowledge)

facts.text: An octopus has three hearts: two pump blood past the gills, and a third pumps it around the rest of the body.
Octopus blood is blue because it carries oxygen with a copper-based protein called hemocyanin instead of iron-based hemoglobin.
Copper-based blood works well in cold, low-oxygen water, which is part of why it suits many deep-sea animals.
The heart that feeds the body stops beating while an octopus swims, which is one reason they tire quickly and prefer to crawl.
An octopus also has nine brains: a central brain plus a small cluster of nerve cells in each of its eight arms.
